"
The search for an Indian tourist, Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, who fell into a sinkhole in Malaysia's capital, Kuala Lumpur, has been suspended. On August 23rd, the pavement she was walking on collapsed, causing her to fall into an eight-meter-deep chasm and vanish from sight.

***

An extensive rescue operation was launched, utilizing advanced aids such as tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar. Rescuers also employed high-pressure water jets to flush the underground drainage system and used excavators to clear away debris in their search for the missing woman.

***

After nearly eight days of continuous effort, the search has yielded little result. Besides her slippers, no other trace of Ms. Gali has been discovered. The country’s fire and rescue department has now officially stalled the operation, concluding that it is too dangerous to proceed.

***

A minister, Dr Zaliha Mustafa, confirmed the halt was due to grave concerns for the safety and health of the rescue personnel. The instability of the site posed a significant threat to anyone entering the sinkhole.
*   Specific dangers noted were an aborted rescue attempt where two divers had to be pulled out before reaching their objective, and the location's history, which includes a reported soil slip last year.

***

Authorities have determined that the hazardous conditions make it unfeasible to continue sending people down into the unstable cavity. This decision was made after the failed dive and in light of the area's prior instability, bringing the rescue efforts to an unfortunate standstill.

Is there anything else I can help with?
